# Branch office WAN uplinks — FigDown source

This is a `topology` figure: two access switches feeding a single branch router, which in turn carries two diverse-path WAN links to separate regional hubs (primary and backup). Genre chosen per the router table — `topology` is the right genre because the content is nodes and links between named network devices, not conditions-with-outcomes (`table`) or a decision path (`flowchart`).

```figdown
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology
title "Branch office WAN uplinks"

class access "Access-layer switch" fill=#e0e7ff stroke=#4338ca
class router "Router" fill=#dcfce7 stroke=#15803d
class hub "Regional hub router" fill=#fef9c3 stroke=#a16207
class primary "Primary WAN path" stroke=#15803d
class backup "Backup / diverse WAN path" stroke=#dc2626 style=dashed

node access1 "Access Switch 1" class=access
node access2 "Access Switch 2" class=access
node branch "Branch Router" class=router
node hubprimary "Regional Hub (Primary)" class=hub
node hubbackup "Regional Hub (Backup, diverse path)" class=hub

edge access1 branch
edge access2 branch
edge branch hubprimary class=primary
edge branch hubbackup class=backup
```

Notes:
- `access1`/`access2`/`branch`/`hubprimary`/`hubbackup` are exactly the ids requested; the four edges are exactly the four links the description states — no additional link (e.g. access1–access2) is drawn, since none was described.
- The `primary`/`backup` classes carry the "diverse-path" and primary-vs-backup meaning in text (per the "class is how meaning survives" rule) rather than relying on colour alone; the dashed style on `backup` is a redundant visual cue, not the sole carrier of that meaning.
- Build/validate with `node build-svg.js branch-wan-uplinks.fd` before embedding; then embed only the resulting SVG in the host document with the standard `source:` footer pointing back at this `.fd`.
